about.title: Maywood Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Maywood is a dense, close-knit community squeezed into just over a square mile of Los Angeles County, where households rely daily on appliances, vehicles, tools, and consumer goods bought locally or shipped in. When one of those products fails — a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a faulty vehicle part, defective machinery on the job, or a mislabeled household chemical — the resulting injury can upend a family fast. California law generally allows injured people to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that defect caused harm. Our team listens to what happened, gathers the basics, and evaluates whether a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer may share responsibility. If you were hurt by a product in Maywood, holding onto the item itself and any packaging can matter later — we can advise you on preserving evidence properly.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Under California law, you often don't need to prove a manufacturer was negligent — showing the product was defective and caused your injury may be enough. Our team can explain how this standard applies to your situation.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held accountable for a defective product. We can help identify which parties were involved in getting that product into your hands.

items.title: No Cost Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront fee to get your claim reviewed. You only owe attorney fees if there's a recovery in your case.

items.question: I still have the product that hurt me — should I keep it?
items.answer: Yes, preserving the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury can be important evidence in a strict liability claim. Try not to alter, repair, or discard it, and keep any packaging, receipts, or instructions if you have them. We can advise you on how to store it properly until it's reviewed.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer knew about the defect?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability framework generally focuses on whether the product itself was defective and caused your injury, not on what the manufacturer knew or intended. This is different from a standard negligence claim and can make certain product cases more straightforward to pursue.

items.question: Does it matter that I live in a small city like Maywood?
items.answer: No — product liability claims are based on where the defective product caused harm, not the size of your city. Whether the injury happened near Slauson Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, or anywhere else in Maywood, we can evaluate your situation the same way.
